text: Kingsmoor FC começou na frente com um pênalti convertido por Viktor Quinlan aos 8 minutos, que tinha uma chance alta de gol (xG 0.76, quase 8 em 10 chances similares resultam em gol) [#152]. Pouco depois, ele marcou novamente em jogada construída com paciência e passes amplos, aumentando para 2-0 [#222]. Mas Westport Albion reagiu rápido com dois gols de Rafael Delacroix, que também teve chances muito boas (xG 0.816 e 0.976) para deixar tudo empatado em 2-2 até os 30 minutos [#401] [#553]. No segundo tempo, Westport virou o jogo aos 51 minutos com Kenji Rahman (xG 0.705) [#983]. Mesmo com um jogador a menos após o cartão vermelho de Felix Barros aos 81', Kingsmoor não desistiu e Luca Iversen empatou com um cruzamento rápido aos 82 minutos (xG 0.888), finalizando em 3-3 [#1495] [#1516]. A partida mostrou as diferenças táticas: Kingsmoor apostou na jogada pelas pontas e cruzamentos, enquanto Westport preferiu passes diretos e rápidos, deixando o jogo mais emocionante até o apito final.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in pt

- Viktor Quinlan scored the opening penalty goal at 8' with xG 0.76, putting Kingsmoor FC ahead 1-0 [#152].
- Westport Albion equalized by 30' thanks to two goals by Rafael Delacroix (xG 0.816 and 0.976) to make it 2-2 [#401, #553].
- Kenji Rahman scored the go-ahead goal for Westport Albion at 51' with xG 0.705, making it 3-2 [#983].
- Felix Barros received a second yellow card red card at 81', reducing Kingsmoor FC to 10 men [#1495].
- Luca Iversen scored the equalizer for Kingsmoor FC at 82' with xG 0.888 assisted by Mason Morales, finalizing the 3-3 draw [#1516].

- Kingsmoor FC’s early goals illustrate effective exploitation of wide areas and crossing play, aligned with their 4-4-2 formation and style emphasizing width. The first goal was a penalty, but the second goal at 12' came after a sustained 8-pass build-up starting from a ball regain, showing patient build-up and quick transition through wide midfielders to create shooting opportunities inside the box [#222].
- Westport Albion responded with goals at 22' and 30' through their characteristic direct, vertical passing style and 4-4-2 formation. Their goals came after regains and involved short passing combinations and crosses into the box, emphasizing quick vertical progression and exploiting spaces behind Kingsmoor’s midfield and defense [#401, #553].
- The pattern for Westport’s equalizer at 30' notably included a cross from Dylan Rahman, fitting their style of direct vertical passing complemented by crossing when progressing into attacking areas [#553]. This contrasts Kingsmoor’s wide but more possession-based approach.
- In the second half, Kingsmoor intensified pressing and directness (press up by 0.18, directness by 0.15, line height +0.12), reflecting an explicit tactical change to chase the game. This increased pressing (lower PPDA) and direct play helped them regain control and create chances despite being down a player later [#1187].
- Westport Albion then reacted by reducing pressing, dropping deeper, and slowing tempo to protect the lead, halving their press and line height ratios. This allowed Kingsmoor more possession (53.3%) but limited Westport’s risk in defensive transitions [#1459].
- The late Kingsmoor equalizer at 82' came from a quick, short passing move after a ball regain, with a low number of touches (2 passes, 8.5s build-up) and a cross assist from Mason Morales, demonstrating Kingsmoor’s wide crossing style used effectively even when under numerical disadvantage after the red card [#1516].
- Overall, the match showcased Kingsmoor’s reliance on wide, crossing opportunities and progressive pressing within their 4-4-2, while Westport used direct vertical passing and quick transitions within a similar formation. The tactical shifts in the second half — Kingsmoor pressing harder and Westport sitting deeper — reflect adaptive responses to match state and scoreline.
